description: Minimal Quartz.NET project with IJob consumers, [DisallowConcurrentExecution], JobBuilder.Create producers, TriggerBuilder, and scheduler.ScheduleJob. Gates the two PRODUCES edges #6741 arm 3 made real for C#: JobBuilder.Create<ReportJob> and JobBuilder.Create<EmailJob> in Startup.cs each reach the IJob class THEY name in jobs/ReportJob.cs — carrying task:quartz.net:<Job> — rather than whichever job class the file declares first, and both bind to the real class entity. This is the only C# fixture where a PRODUCES edge is graded must_exist. Deliberately no CONSUMES: as of #6741 arm 5 nothing in the tree emits that kind, in any language (known gap, recorded in ADR-0028). The TRIGGERS rows below stay nice_to_have because no such edge is emitted here either.

expected_relationships.note: #6490 arm B. `class Startup { Task ConfigureScheduler(IScheduler scheduler) }`.
Second class in the same file — the CONTAINS must not be hoisted onto ReportJob.
The job-class view of the same declaration, emitted by the Quartz.NET framework pass.
`var reportJob = JobBuilder.Create<ReportJob>()...Build();` — the generic type argument names the job class being built.
`var trigger = TriggerBuilder.Create()...Build();` — external Quartz.NET API, so a bare-name target is the correct shape.
`await scheduler.ScheduleJob(reportJob, trigger);` resolved through the declared parameter type IScheduler.

#6741 arm 3. `JobBuilder.Create<ReportJob>()` in Startup.cs dispatches the IJob declared in jobs/ReportJob.cs. ADR-0028 §1's one-hop degenerate form: producer -> job class, carrying `task:quartz.net:ReportJob` as a property. Cross-file, so the edge targets the resolvable `Class:ReportJob` stub the C# passes already use for out-of-file types.
The second builder must pair with the type IT names, not with whichever job class happens to come first.

#6490 arm B FINDING: the fixture asserts a `scheduler.ScheduleJob` schedule_job ENTITY (and it is extracted), but nothing points at it — the CALLS from the enclosing method goes to the bare name `IScheduler.ScheduleJob` instead. The schedule_job entity is a graph orphan.

#6742: `public class ReportJob : IJob`. Promoted from nice_to_have when C# class-hierarchy extraction landed. This is the C# half of the language-parity pair — java-quartz-mini asserts `SendEmailJob IMPLEMENTS Job` for the structurally identical declaration, and internal/extractors/hierarchy_parity_6742_test.go fails if the two languages ever disagree on the KIND.

#6742: the second job class in the same file gets its own edge. Held constant against the row above: same file, same supertype, same kind — the axis varied is the owning declaration, which is what a base list hoisted onto the file's first type would get wrong.

#6490 arm B FINDING: `scheduler.ScheduleJob(reportJob, trigger)` registers ReportJob with the scheduler, and no edge of any kind connects the two. Since #6741 arm 3 the graph does contain the two PRODUCES edges above, emitted by the JobBuilder producers; TRIGGERS is still zero here, and CONSUMES is zero everywhere in the tree because nothing emits it (ADR-0028) — contrast java-quartz-mini, which does emit a TRIGGERS edge for the same pattern in Java.

#6490 arm B FINDING: the `report-trigger` entity is extracted with no edges at all. `TriggerBuilder.Create().WithIdentity("report-trigger")` is passed to ScheduleJob alongside reportJob; the trigger→job association is in the source and absent from the graph.

forbidden_relationships.note: #6742 KIND GUARD. IJob is an interface, so the edge is IMPLEMENTS. Recall cannot see this: emitting BOTH kinds, or the wrong one alongside the right one, still satisfies every must_exist row above. Only a forbidden row grades the kind exclusively — and the kind is the whole point of the parity with java-quartz-mini.

#6742: `class Startup` has NO base list. `Task ConfigureScheduler(IScheduler scheduler)` names IScheduler as a parameter type only. A predicate that reached for any type mentioned near a declaration rather than for the base_list node would land here.
